```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

`VariationalBayesHLRM` uses one typed fitting interface for LRM, HLRM, and
CHLRM. The model, prior, initialization strategy, and inference control are
separate objects.

```{r}
library(VariationalBayesHLRM)
set.seed(101)
X <- cbind(intercept = 1, predictor = seq(-2, 2, length.out = 30))
data <- list(X = X, y = drop(X %*% c(1, 1.5)) + rnorm(30, sd = 0.5))
prior <- lrm_prior(c(0, 0), 10 * diag(2), 4, 1)

fit <- fit_model(
  lrm_model(2), data, prior, method = "cavi",
  initialization = initialization_ols(),
  control = cavi_control(max_iterations = 200),
  seed = 102, verbose = FALSE
)

fit
fit$diagnostics$status
coef(fit)
plot(fit, type = "convergence")
plot(fit, type = "coefficients")
draws <- posterior_draws(fit, n_draws = 200, seed = 105)
plot(draws, parameter = "coefficients")
```

MCMC convergence is based on multiple-chain R-hat, ESS, and MCSE. CAVI uses
full-data ELBO and parameter stabilization. SVI evaluates comparable full-data
objectives periodically and never treats unrelated minibatch objectives as a
stopping sequence. Consequently, all engines return the same convergence
contract but only applicable metrics.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
mcmc_fit <- fit_model(
  lrm_model(2), data, prior, method = "mcmc",
  initialization = initialization_ols(),
  control = mcmc_control(
    warmup = 1000, post_warmup_draws = 2000, chains = 4,
    stopping = mcmc_stopping()
  ),
  seed = 103, verbose = FALSE
)

svi_fit <- fit_model(
  lrm_model(2), data, prior, method = "svi",
  initialization = initialization_ols(),
  control = svi_control(
    max_iterations = 20000, minibatch_size = 10,
    learning_rate = power_schedule(offset = 100, exponent = 0.7),
    stopping = svi_stopping()
  ),
  seed = 104, verbose = FALSE
)
```


## History-free restart primitives

For applications that manage immutable draw blocks separately, a complete MCMC
fit can supply current sampler and per-chain RNG states without retaining its
past histories in the returned object. Advance one chain at a time, preserve
both the returned draw block and next state, and make scientific decisions only
after a complete matched chain prefix. These operations never repeat warm-up or
reseed continuation, and they preserve the caller's RNG. They require Inversion
normal generation, including when recovering a saved stream.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
state <- mcmc_restart_state(mcmc_fit)
block <- advance_mcmc_state(state, additional_samples = 5000, chain = 1,
                            max_memory_mb = 512)
# Persist block$draws and block$draw_index in the application's history store.
save_mcmc_restart_state(block$state, "restart-002.state")
next_state <- read_mcmc_restart_state("restart-002.state")

# Existing immutable object-store checkpoints support selective state recovery.
# This does not decode their historical draw chunks.
state <- read_mcmc_restart_state("checkpoint-001.rds",
                                 format = "checkpoint_store")
```

The context preserves extraction-time model/prior/scaling specifications. Current
retained iteration counts are in each chain's `run_settings$samples`. Returned
native draws have raw labels and use the sampler's working scale. This is a
low-level state/block API, not a complete disk-backed posterior reporting engine
or a convergence certificate. Keep the original full checkpoint/history, and
use existing typed fitted objects for their posterior reports. Resource guards
bound an analytical active-state/block allowance; they do not guarantee OS RSS.


## Immutable native draw history

A complete object-store checkpoint can become a baseline for an immutable
history. Subsequent generations store new blocks and current restart state,
without reconstructing or rewriting old arrays. Keep the baseline checkpoint
and its object store: the history references that dependency by checksum and
relative path. Relocating a history requires preserving the dependency tree.

```{r, eval=FALSE}
save_mcmc_checkpoint(mcmc_fit, "baseline.rds", "baseline-store")
history <- create_mcmc_history("baseline.rds", "native-history")
state <- mcmc_history_restart_state(history)
block <- advance_mcmc_state(state, additional_samples = 500, chain = 1,
                            max_memory_mb = 512)
next_history <- append_mcmc_history(history, block)
selected <- mcmc_history_draws(next_history, chain = 1,
  iterations = c(1, 100, 2001, 2500), fields = c("Beta", "logjoint"))
# Old snapshots remain readable; reload after an interrupted append.
latest_history <- read_mcmc_history("native-history")
```

Reads retain native parameter names, working scale, raw component labels and
original per-chain iteration identities. They do not align labels, restore a
fitted-model object, compute posterior predictions, or certify convergence.
CHLRM's new blocks verify group histories exactly against component draws and
allocations, then store an equivalent derived representation; reads reconstruct
those group values without altering samples. Existing baseline arrays remain
intact. Requested-output and decoded-chunk guards are analytical allowances,
not operating-system RSS guarantees. A large historical baseline chunk may
require an explicit larger chunk allowance; it is never silently truncated.

Append is single-writer, rejects stale or mismatched parent states, and publishes
a new immutable snapshot only after all dependencies exist. Failed publication
leaves older snapshots valid and may leave unreferenced objects. No automatic
resampling, sampling retry, or garbage collection occurs. Separate chain
frontiers do not qualify as a complete matched prefix for joint diagnostics.
